title: Fixture Foundry
tagline: Setup and teardown that runs even when the test explodes.
teaches: conftest.py, fixtures, yield, scope, and why cleanup belongs after the yield
objectives: Explain what pytest does when it sees an argument name it recognises as a fixture
Write a fixture that yields, and put the cleanup where a failing test cannot skip it
Choose a scope on purpose - function, module, session - and say what you traded away
Put a fixture in conftest.py so every test in the folder can use it without importing anything
Name the one thing a fixture must never do: leave the next test a page it did not ask for
plannedChallenges: Your first fixture: a logged-in session
yield, and the cleanup that always runs
Fix the broken test: teardown that never fires because the test failed first
Scope: why session-scoped state is a loaded gun
Move it to conftest.py and delete the import
Boss: build the fixture that creates a user and deletes it afterwards, whatever happens
